title: Drug-induced atrioventricular block: prognosis after discontinuation of the culprit drug
authors: Zeltser D, Justo D, Halkin A, Rosso R, Ish-Shalom M, Hochenberg M, et al.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
population: Consecutive patients with second- or third-degree atrioventricular block not related to acute myocardial infarction, digitalis toxicity or vasovagal syncope, at Tel Aviv-Sourasky Medical Center
funder: not read: the full text requires a subscription and is absent from PubMed Central.
result: Of 169 patients, 92 (54%) were taking beta-blockers, verapamil or diltiazem, with clinical and electrocardiographic characteristics similar to those without such drugs. Stopping the drug was followed by resolution of the block in 41%, against spontaneous improvement in 23% of patients without drugs, but block recurred without therapy in 56% of those whose block had resolved. Block truly caused by the drugs was found in only 15% of patients who developed second- or third-degree block on these drugs.
